title: Session pin, retry calibration, and generator sugar
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Minor SDK ergonomics and parity fixes across Python/TypeScript/Go: session pinning flag, tuned retry/backoff presets, and a lightweight generator/async-iterator helper. Non-breaking API surface; bump patch versions.
description:
Context: Multiple internal teams were hitting transient 401/429 spikes during long-lived streaming sessions and observed divergent retry behavior across our Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs. This PR introduces a small cross-SDK convergence: a session pin parameter to keep a long-lived session affinity option, calibrated retry/backoff presets tuned for streaming heartbeats, and a lightweight generator/async-iterator sugar to make streaming ergonomics simpler for application code.

What this changes (single-string summary):
- Add `session_pin` (optional) to client/session constructors (Py/TS/Go). When set, SDKs attach a short-lived session pin header and extend token refresh grace for the bound session. The flag is opt-in and defaults to false.
- Introduce `retry_profiles.streaming_tolerant` with calibrated backoff floors/ceilings tuned for long polling and server-initiated stream heartbeats. Profiles are small and composable; SDKs fall back to existing presets if not supplied.
- Add `generator_sugar` helpers: Python `stream_generator()`, TypeScript `createAsyncGeneratorStream()`, Go `StreamGenerator()` that wrap lower-level transport and expose a consistent, typed async-iterator/pull-stream interface. These helpers are intentionally tiny and documented with examples.
- Align telemetry tags emitted by the client during reauth/retry: `sdk.session_pin`, `sdk.retry_profile`, and `sdk.stream_helper` so observability dashboards can be correlated across languages.
- Docs and examples: quickstart short examples in each SDK showing `session_pin` usage and generator helper.

Motivation: Services with infrequent token rotations and lots of small streaming reads saw noisy client-side reconnect loops because SDKs applied different backoff defaults and reauth windows. The session pin reduces churn for sticky streams; the calibrated retry profile reduces high-frequency reconnection storms while being conservative for real outages. The generator sugar reduces copy-paste in user code and ensures cross-sdk parity for common patterns.

Compatibility: No breaking changes. `session_pin` is optional. Retry profiles are additive. Generator helpers are thin wrappers; existing streaming APIs remain available. Version bumps: python SDK +0.0.5, typescript SDK +0.0.6, go SDK +0.0.3 (patch-level sync).

Checklist: [x] Unit tests for new helpers (Py/TS/Go) [x] Integration test that simulates token rollover with `session_pin` [x] Telemetry tags verified in local e2e run [x] Docs snippets updated [x] Version bumps applied to each SDK manifest

High-level commits: see commits list below.

Notes for reviewers: the change is intentionally conservative. Focus review on: backoff numbers in `retry_profiles.streaming_tolerant`, the header format for `session_pin` (we use `X-Session-Pin: <hex>`), and that generator helpers surface the same error semantics across languages (no implicit swallowing of transport errors).

Follow-ups (not in this PR): a small follow-up will add a CLI flag in the private installer to toggle session pin behavior for on-prem deployments and an ops doc for interpreting the new telemetry tags.
